set_aside.subject: existing staff-assignment schema
set_aside.text:
(`staff_id`, `project_id`) is unique among active assignments only, so the
revoked ones of a pair stay (A3 INV-009).
set_aside.question: When the caller's open database already has the former full UNIQUE constraint on (`staff_id`, `project_id`), must this operation reject the incompatible schema, require a separately migrated schema as a precondition, or alter it despite “never drops, alters”?
options: Declare a compatible current-revision schema as an input precondition and assign migration to deploy.
Detect the former constraint and fail with a specified schema-incompatibility failure until deploy migrates it.
Permit this operation to migrate the constraint, revising the promise that it never alters tables.
set_aside.default_guess: Require a compatible schema revision, have deploy migrate older databases, and make this operation fail explicitly when it detects an incompatible existing table.

witness.initial: The caller owns an open database whose assignment table was created under the previously closed contract with UNIQUE (`staff_id`, `project_id`) and contains a revoked assignment for one pair.
events: module:portal_store calls create_staff_access_schema on that connection.
An administrator later assigns the same staff_id to the same project_id again.
outcomes: The output obligation requires storage that permits the new active assignment while retaining the revoked assignment.
The state-impact obligation “never drops, alters” leaves the former full UNIQUE constraint in place, so the new assignment cannot be inserted.
witness.observer: module:portal_store and the administrator attempting the reassignment
